title: Scope — Circle Drawer's circles as virtual nodes

data.head: # Scope — Circle Drawer's circles as virtual nodes

body:
Working entry (`chk-i5hwelaf`, Epoch 4 — Inside the canvas): «Circle Drawer's circles as virtual nodes — each circle a
node, its draw commands grouped by it, with stand checks (v040-10, v040-11)», with seven CARRYs folded below.

- Circle Drawer's canvas widget (`CircleCanvas` in `examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/circle_drawer.rs`) declares one
  virtual node per circle it paints through `Widget::virtual_nodes`: an author key, an AccessKit role, a non-empty name
  and a region in its content box. Circle Drawer becomes the first served app to declare virtual nodes, so each circle
  reads as a node — `{owner}///{key}` — in the accessibility tree, the snapshot, the diff, the UI graph, `actions`,
  `layout` and exploration, as the three earlier chunks built them on fixture canvases.

- `click` on a circle's node acts on its circle and its diff names it; a covered, off-screen, disabled or removed
  circle node is refused with that cause (v040-11's acceptance, on the stand).

- The canvas reading (`Session::canvas`, the `canvas` verb) groups a canvas's draw commands under the virtual node that
  covers them (v040-10's last open clause), and a changed command reads with an identity in the reading's diff (CARRY 1).
- Stand checks in both layout modes, and the binary-level reading of a virtual node's id and name (CARRY 4).
- Keyboard reach of the circles is «Canvas keyboard path»'s, the next entry — not built here.
- A rotated or scaled canvas's virtual nodes are «Pan and zoom»'s (its own CARRY) — not built here.

- The lint's label-overlap, label-contrast, command-outside-region and zero-area-shape readings stay their residuals'
  (res-zahb4t5s, res-afru4fnu, res-6djljwev, res-5aosveco) unless a CARRY below takes one.

data.head: # Plan — 2026-11-25-circle-drawer-virtual-nodes: "Circle Drawer's circles as virtual nodes"

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-11-25-circle-drawer-virtual-nodes · **Version:** escher-0.4.0
- **Base:** HEAD `a5d18f604a88533232d9164b5db1afd3e6159070` when P4 wrote this plan.

- **Answers:** the forks F1–F9 of `evidence/founder-forks.md`, answered as the operator's: F1 A, F2 B, F3 A, F4 A, F5 B,
  F6 A, F7 A and F8 with role `Image` by the escher overseer (inputs#I2, a delegate's word); F5 B rests on the founder's
  own F13 A, which names the coverage line among the reads that carry a virtual id (inputs#I3); F9 B by the operator in
  this session (inputs#I4).

Circle Drawer, the stand's one canvas app, declares each circle it paints as a virtual node. Each circle reads as
`circle-canvas///c{id}` in the accessibility tree, the snapshot and its diff, the UI graph, `actions`, `layout` and
exploration, the reads the three earlier chunks built on fixture canvases. Its role is `Image` and its name
«Circle {id}, {d} px». Its region is its bounding square cut to the canvas's content box (inputs#I2, F8). Its key comes from an id the
app gives each circle, never its index (security-plan · contract/stable-element-id/stability). The `data-circles`
attribute carries that id as a fourth field. The app's click is unchanged (F1 A): a click on a circle's node adds a
circle at its centre, a limit stated and witnessed.

The `canvas` verb's full answer groups every command under the virtual node that covers it (v040-10's last open clause,
CARRY 1). Each line ends ` n={k}`, the 1-based index of the node among the canvas's taken nodes in declaration order, or
` n=-` for none. Only numbers enter the ratified canvas crossing; no id or name does (F2 B; security-plan ·
decision/canvas-content-crossing). A changed command's removed and added lines carry one `n=`, which names its node; the
index is positional, a stated limit.

Handler coverage lists `click` under each virtual node's own id, owned by its canvas, wherever the canvas holds a `click`
listener. It reads exercised where a replayed accepted `click` named that id (F5 B on the founder's F13 A). The graph is
unchanged: a virtual node carries no handler there (F14 A).

blitz-dom re-exports the role type beside `VirtualNodeDeclaration`, behind `custom-widget`: an escher addition to the
engine crate's public surface. An app that declares a virtual node then names its role from the crate that defines the
declaration, with no manifest or lock move (F9 B, inputs#I4).

The CARRYs are all decided. CARRY 1 is built by the grouping, and CARRY 5 by its fix. CARRY 6 is built by coverage
(F5 B). CARRYs 2, 3 and 7 stay as stated limits, each witnessed on the stand (F3 A, F4 A, F6 A). CARRY 4 moves to
«Cold-agent live run»: Circle Drawer is served by no role (F7 A). Literal pins are swept (inputs#I1).

1. **The role type re-exported (F9 B).** In `packages/blitz-dom/src/lib.rs`, beside `pub use
   crate::node::VirtualNodeDeclaration` (`:107-108`), add a `#[cfg(feature = "custom-widget")]` re-export of
   `accesskit::Role` as `VirtualNodeRole`. Its `///` doc says it is the type a declaration's `role` takes, re-exported
   so an app declaring a virtual node names it from this crate, an escher addition flagged upstreamable. The field
   `VirtualNodeDeclaration.role` keeps its type (`custom_widget.rs:182`). No manifest line changes (keeps arch S5).

2. **A circle's id.** In `examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/circle_drawer.rs`:
   - `Circle` gains an `id: u64`, and `CircleDrawer` keeps a counter of the next id as a graph signal
     (`use_graph_signal`), written by the canvas's click (declared `writes("circle-canvas", "click")`, so the graph
     reads no flag).
   - A click gives its new circle the counter's value, from 1, and moves the counter.
   - Undo and redo keep a circle's id, since they restore whole vectors. A circle a click adds after an undo takes a
     fresh id, never a reused one.
   - `circles_text` (`:25`) writes `x,y,d,id` per circle.
   - `Painted` gains the id, and `parse_circles` (`:43`) reads exactly four fields: three finite numbers and an id that
     parses as a whole number from 1. Any other entry, a three-field one included, reads as no circle.
   - The unit table `malformed_circle_text_reads_as_no_circle` (`:435`) is restated in four-field rows, its row count
     asserted, with a three-field row and an id of 0 among the malformed rows (keeps tests S4–S5).

4. **Commands grouped by node (F2 B, CARRY 1).** In `packages/escher-driver/src/canvas.rs`:
   - `Session::canvas` (`:270`) reads the canvas's declared nodes through `DioxusDocument::virtual_nodes`. A read that
     answers `NoCanvas` or `NotLaidOut` groups nothing.
   - The regions and the paint scale are handed to `read_commands` (`:305`).
   - Each command's bounds are read in the scene's frame and divided by the scale into CSS px of the content box. A
     fill or stroke uses its shape's bounding box under its transform, a glyph run the box of its glyph origins under
     its transform, a box shadow and an image their rect.
   - A command belongs to the taken node whose region holds the centre of its bounds and whose region's centre lies
     nearest it, ties to the first declared. A layer push or pop, or a command with no area or whose centre no region
     holds, belongs to none.
   - The reading carries each command's node as a 1-based index into the taken nodes in declaration order, or none.
   
   In `packages/escher-driver/src/json/canvas.rs`, `canvas_lines` (`:255`) ends every line ` n={k}` or ` n=-` after
   its form, in every canvas answer, declaring or not. `canvas_line_lengths` (`:280`) counts the tag, so parts still
   cut within the budget. The summary is unchanged. The command span and every log stay as they are
   (obs-plan · decision/canvas-read-opens-no-span, architecture · contract/command-span/never-fielded).

5. **The canvas reading's tests.**
   - `packages/escher-driver/src/json_tests.rs`: `every_canvas_command_kind_and_brush_form_is_written_once` restates its
     lines with the tag.
   - `packages/escher-driver/src/canvas_tests.rs` gains a table-driven case of the grouping rule, its row count
     asserted. The rows: a command in one region; in two, the nearer centre winning; a tie read as the first declared;
     in none; a layer line; a scale of 2.

6. **Coverage by virtual node (F5 B, CARRY 6).** In `packages/escher-driver/src/coverage.rs`:
   - `see` lists `click` for each graph node whose id holds `///` and whose owner's graph node carries a `click`
     handler, with `id` the virtual id and `owner` the canvas's id.
   - `handler_coverage` marks a virtual node's `click` reached where a replayed step is an accepted `click` naming its
     id, read off the check's own steps.
   - A click on the canvas's id that lands inside a node's region counts the canvas's listener alone, a stated limit.
   - The module doc (`:9-12`) is restated. The coverage line keeps its form: ids, owner ids, event names and two
     counts (security-plan · decision/coverage-line-no-user-data).
   - The graph (`DioxusDocument::graph`) is not touched (F14 A).

7. **The stand check, new** — `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_circle_nodes.rs`, one behaviour: Circle Drawer's circles
   as virtual nodes, both layout modes. Its tables are shared in `tests/blitz-tests/tests/common/mod.rs`, each with its
   row count asserted. It asserts its fixture's condition first (keeps arch S1–S5, tests S1–S5, a11y S1–S2, security
   S1–S2, obs S2/S4). Its cases:
   - (a) After one click, the canvas's accessibility node holds the child `circle-canvas///c1` with role `Image`, label
     «Circle 1, 40 px» and that author id. The snapshot reads it with `bounds` equal to its region moved by the canvas's
     content origin. The canvas summary reads `width` 700 and `height` 400, the step-3 constants.
   - (b) At 12 and at 100 circles of the fixture sequence (step 9's form), the snapshot lists 12 and 100 such nodes.
     None is refused: `virtual_nodes`' `refused` is empty. Each of the 3 circles that spill the box at 100 reads its
     cut region.
   - (c) Id stability: two clicks with an `advance` between read `c1` and `c2`. An undo takes `c2` away, and a click
     naming it is refused `stale`. A redo brings `c2` back under the same id. A click after another undo reads `c3`.
     An id no screen read is refused `not-found`.
   - (d) Diffs: a click's diff adds the new node. A resize through the dialog changes `c1`, its diff naming `name` and
     `bounds` in `differs`.
   - (e) F1 A witness: a `click` on `circle-canvas///c1` is accepted, settles and adds a circle at its centre. Its diff
     adds `c2` and leaves `c1` unchanged.
   - (f) F4 A witness: with `c1` under `c2` at the centre, a click on `c1` is not refused `covered`.
   - (g) The other reads on Circle Drawer:
     - the UI graph holds each `c{id}` node, owned by `circle-canvas`, with no handlers or reads;
     - `actions` lists each with `click` and `layout` free of a cause, and `type`, `scroll`, `screenshot` and `canvas`
       `not-found`;
     - `layout` answers it placed `by: app` in `circle-canvas`;
     - an in-process `explore` with a budget of 40 reaches a path whose call clicks a `c{id}` id.
     
     The graph, actions and layout answers hold the id and never the name «Circle 1, 40 px».
   - (h) F6 A witness: at 12 and 100 fixture circles the lint reads no finding, and no finding id holds `///`.
   - (i) F3 A witness: the fixture's smallest circle at 100 (diameter under 14 px, 5 measured) has a label wider than its
     circle, and it reads no `truncated` finding: the label's region is the content box.
   - (j) The grouping:
     - After one click, the full answer's fill, stroke and glyph lines end ` n=1` and its layer lines ` n=-`.
     - At 12 and 100 fixture circles, each circle's fill, stroke and glyph lines end with its own index, for 12 of 12
       and 100 of 100 circles.
     - A resize's line diff holds only removed and added lines carrying ` n=1`: identity by node.
     - Positional limit witness: after an undo of `c2` and a new click, the new circle `c3` reads ` n=2`, the index `c2`
       held.
   - (k) F5 B: a kept check on Circle Drawer clicks `circle-canvas///c1` after two canvas clicks. `handler_coverage`
     over it lists `circle-canvas///c2` `click`, owner `circle-canvas`, unexercised, and lists neither `c1`'s `click`
     nor the canvas's `click`. A second check clicking only the canvas lists both nodes' `click` unexercised (unix, as
     every recording check, tests S6 / test-plan history `amd-xliprnr6`).

8. **CARRY 5 and the coverage case.** In `tests/blitz-tests/tests/virtual_nodes_in_every_read.rs`:
   - The `session_common` import's `snapshot` (`:24`) moves behind `#[cfg(unix)]`, its one use being the
     `#[cfg(unix)]` case at `:399-437`.
   - `a_replayed_virtual_click_reaches_its_canvas_listener` is restated for F5 B. Its kept check's replayed click on a
     virtual id reads that id's `click` exercised and the canvas's listener reached under the canvas's id. A second
     declared node not clicked reads its `click` unexercised.

9. **The fixture sequence's form.** `tests/blitz-tests/tests/session_common/mod.rs`'s `circles` (`:797`) writes
   `x,y,d,k`, `k` the circle's place in the sequence from 1. Its doc and `draw`'s doc say so.

10. **The literal pins swept.** These are the `data-circles` literals and every pin a Circle Drawer reading moves, each
    re-measured, never forecast:
    - `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_circle_drawer_canvas.rs:118` → `"348,198,40,1"`, `:207` →
      `"348,198,40,1;348,198,40,2"`, `:211` → `"348,198,53,1;348,198,40,2"` (the sweep `git grep -nE
      '"[0-9.]+,[0-9.]+,[0-9.]+(;[0-9.,]+)*"' -- tests examples packages docs`: 4 hits, 3 changed, 1 no-change —
      `blitz-vibey-script/tests/seeded_random.rs:39`, random numbers, not a circle).
    - `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_canvas_commands.rs`'s 17-row `TABLE`: every full and part row's size and digest
      moves by the tag. Predicted: each line +4 to +5 bytes, the 100-circle dump at 6 parts; record what the re-run
      measures, on linux here and on windows and macOS by the CI read.
    - `tests/blitz-tests/tests/common/mod.rs`'s `UNEXERCISED_AFTER_DRIVES` Circle Drawer row (`:460`). Predicted: it gains
      the `click` of each circle node the drives leave on a screen; record what `stand_handler_coverage` measures.
    - `docs/capabilities.md`'s dump sizes (`:322`, 45 · 527 · 5,915 · 49,266) re-measured.
    - Predicted unmoved, read by the gates:
      - `stand_canvas_cross_os`' Circle Drawer digest `0x5d5664142f9a5201`: the paint is unchanged;
      - `stand_canvas_lint` and `stand_lint`: no finding on a virtual node;
      - `stand_non_lean_tasks`' counts: it counts elements;
      - `stand_graph`'s reserved-separator walk: it reads Circle Drawer at boot, with no circle;
      - `stand_cross_os_readings`: it does not read Circle Drawer.

11. **The capability statement.** In `docs/capabilities.md`:
    - The canvas section states the ` n=` tag, the grouping rule and its positional limit.
    - The virtual-node section names Circle Drawer's circles with their key, role, name and region.
    - The stated limits are added or restated: a click on a circle's node adds a circle (F1 A); `covered` by elements
      alone (F4 A, `«A virtual node's covered»` kept); a label's region is the content box (F3 A); the lint holds no
      virtual node (F6 A); coverage counts a node's click only for a click naming it (F5 B).
    - The verb and cause names and the five counts are unmoved: `test_capability_statement.py` reads them.

12. **The controls**, implement's one-shot runs through `gate.py control`, each entered with its red reading:
    - C1: `CircleCanvas::virtual_nodes` returns an empty list → `stand_circle_nodes`'s
      `one_click_reads_a_circle_node_in_the_tree_and_the_snapshot` red.
    - C2: the region cut removed (the bounding square declared whole) → `at_twelve_and_a_hundred_circles_every_circle_reads_a_node` red, 3 refused at 100.
    - C3: the key from the circle's index in the list → `an_undone_circle_reads_stale_and_its_redo_keeps_its_id` red.
    - C4: the grouping's tie and nearest-centre rule replaced by «the last declared region holding the centre» →
      `each_circle_s_commands_carry_its_own_index` red (69 of 100 on the fixture, measured off-tree).
    - C5: `see`'s virtual-node arm removed → `a_kept_check_lists_the_unclicked_circle_s_click` red and
      `a_replayed_virtual_click_reaches_its_canvas_listener` red.
    - C6: `parse_circles` taking three fields again → `malformed_circle_text_reads_as_no_circle` red.
    
    Each names the file and the text the edit removes and its `case` by function name, and is reached past fail-fast
    by a `--test` filter (keeps tests S4, test-plan · decision/mutation-controlled-tests).

13. **The CARRY 5 check:** `cargo check --tests --locked --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu -p blitz-tests` reads no
    `unused import` warning (a gate entry), as `testing.md` 2026-10-19 calls for.
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_circle_nodes.rs` — Circle Drawer's circles as virtual nodes on the stand, both layout modes (step 7)
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/lib.rs` — the role type re-exported behind custom-widget (step 1)
- `examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/circle_drawer.rs` — a circle's id, the four-field attribute, the declared nodes (steps 2–3)
- `packages/escher-driver/src/canvas.rs` — commands grouped by node (step 4)
- `packages/escher-driver/src/json/canvas.rs` — the line tag (step 4)
- `packages/escher-driver/src/json_tests.rs` — the line table (step 5)
- `packages/escher-driver/src/canvas_tests.rs` — the grouping rule's table (step 5)
- `packages/escher-driver/src/coverage.rs` — a virtual node's click (step 6)
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/virtual_nodes_in_every_read.rs` — CARRY 5 and the coverage case (step 8)
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/session_common/mod.rs` — the fixture sequence's form (step 9)
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/common/mod.rs` — the new check's tables and the drives' coverage row (steps 7, 10)
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_circle_drawer_canvas.rs` — the three `data-circles` literals (step 10)
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_canvas_commands.rs` — the committed table re-measured (step 10)
- `docs/capabilities.md` — sizes and stated limits (steps 10–11)
**The gates:**
- a probe that no manifest or lock changed, from the base `a5d18f604`;
- the `--locked` workspace build;
- the three crates' unit tests;
- the new target, the edited virtual-node target and its two siblings;
- the stand companions that read Circle Drawer, the canvas, coverage, the graph and the carriers;
- the windows check for CARRY 5;
- the `a11y` leg, which runs `virtual_nodes_as_elements`;
- the `stand-repeat` leg, which takes the new `stand_` file by its glob;
- the pre-push gate (`fast`), which runs the CI-script tests, `test_capability_statement` among them;
- the `doc` leg, because step 1 adds a public item with a doc and step 4 restates doc comments.
**What is absent:**

- There is no boot-path touchpoint (no binary's start changes; Circle Drawer stays served by no role, F7 A), so no
  smoke entry.
- There is no live leg (a live run is «Cold-agent live run»'s), and no headful self-verify harness in this project.
- There is no `audit` leg: the probe holds every manifest and the lock unchanged.

- The coverage leg is not run locally. CI's coverage job reads the escher-driver floor on the pushed tree, and the CI
  read asserts green over it.

**The controls** are step 12's one-shot runs. The diff moves one OS-conditional site, step 8's import behind
`#[cfg(unix)]`, which the windows check and the CI read name.

- (tests · v040-10, matrix#v040-10) On the stand, `canvas` answers Circle Drawer's draw commands at a summary and a full
  level. Two reads give the same bytes, and the answers equal `stand_canvas_commands`' committed table on linux,
  windows and macOS (the CI read).
  - A click's line diff adds the new circle's lines, each ending ` n={its index}`, and removes none.
  - A resize's diff names its circle by the shared ` n=` of each removed and added line.
  - Every command is grouped under the virtual node whose region holds its centre and lies nearest it: 12 of 12 and 100
    of 100 fixture circles read their own index (`stand_circle_nodes`).
  - The canvas lint names a planted label overflowing its region and reads clean on the stand (`stand_canvas_lint`).
  - The 100-circle dump's size is stated in `docs/capabilities.md`.
  - The ratified crossing holds on every carrier: the tag is a number or `-`, and no answer holds an id or name
    (`stand_canvas_carriers`, `stand_masks_on_new_answers`).
  
  Witnessed by the `stand_circle_nodes` and companion entries and the CI read (per security-plan ·
  decision/canvas-content-crossing, architecture · decision/canvas-reading-diffable).

- (a11y · stand) Each Circle Drawer circle reads as `circle-canvas///c{id}`, role `Image`, named «Circle {id}, {d} px»,
  its bounds its cut region, in the accessibility tree and the snapshot. At 12 and 100 circles none is refused
  (`stand_circle_nodes` a–b; a11y-plan · decision/snapshot-reads-the-tree).

- (security) A circle's key is its app-given id, stable across undo and redo: a removed circle is refused `stale`, and
  an unknown id `not-found` (`stand_circle_nodes` c; security-plan · contract/stable-element-id/stability).

- (arch) The UI graph, `actions`, `layout` and exploration read the circles on the stand with the id and never the
  name (`stand_circle_nodes` g; security-plan · decision/virtual-node-crossing).

- (arch · CARRY 6) Handler coverage lists a circle node's `click` under its own id, owned by `circle-canvas`. The click
  is exercised where a replayed click named it, and the canvas's listener is counted under the canvas's id
  (`stand_circle_nodes` k, `virtual_nodes_in_every_read`; F5 B on F13 A, inputs#I3).

- (tests · CARRY 5) `cargo check --tests --locked --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu -p blitz-tests` reads no unused import,
  and the CI read's windows leg is green.

- (tests) Every gate entry above reads green, and each of controls C1–C6 enters with its red reading
  (test-plan · decision/mutation-controlled-tests).
- (security · F9 B) No manifest or lock line changes (the probe). The role type reaches the app from blitz-dom.

- v040-11 is not claimed: its keyboard reach is «Canvas keyboard path»'s, and its click clause and `covered` / `off-screen`
  / `disabled` stand readings wait on that entry's selection (F1 A, inputs#I2).
- The standing lists kept: arch S1–S5, tests S1–S6, security S1–S3, a11y S1–S3, obs S1–S4, design S3, layouts S1.

- Research files inspected: those listed in `doc:2026-11-25-circle-drawer-virtual-nodes/research` (rev 1), and
  `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_circle_drawer_canvas.rs`, `stand_non_lean_tasks.rs`, `stand_handler_coverage.rs`,
  `stand_requirement_sweep.rs` read at P4.

- Inputs: inputs#I1 (the take-up direction), inputs#I2 (the answers to F1–F8), inputs#I3 (the founder's F13 A),
  inputs#I4 (F9 B).
- A seven_guis `accesskit` dependency — rejected on F9 B: a lock move, and the role type belongs with the declaration.

- An index key — rejected: security-plan · contract/stable-element-id/stability forbids it, and an undo would hand a
  removed circle's key to the next.

- A node's id or key in the canvas answer — rejected on F2 B: a widening of a ratified crossing, the founder's
  (F2 C/D).

- The last-declared or first-declared covering region as the grouping rule — rejected: on the fixture they group 69 and
  56 of 100 circles under their own node, and the last-declared moves earlier tags on a click.

- A tag only on a declaring canvas — rejected: Circle Drawer's boot answer would gain tags at its first click and the
  click's diff would remove its layer lines.

- A virtual node's handler in the UI graph — rejected: F14 A keeps the graph unchanged, and coverage alone lists the
  click.

- Serving Circle Drawer, a live run, a lint reading of virtual nodes, a sibling `covered`, a label region by node, a
  click that selects — each not built here (F7 A, F6 A, F4 A, F3 A, F1 A).

- No plan step deletes a worktree or a build directory (inputs#I2). A probe worktree goes outside `target/`. A guard
  refusal of a write is a stop. No raw log holding a temp or home path enters evidence (inputs#I1).
- A lock move met during implement stops the run (inputs#I2).

- The canvas summary's 700 × 400 is asserted, never assumed. If it reads otherwise, step 3's constants follow the
  measured box and the CSS stays.

- `stand_requirement_sweep`'s `WITNESSES` table holds the 0.1.0 requirements alone (16 rows,
  `stand_requirement_sweep.rs:250`). No v040 row is added here; the version's witness rows are its close's.

- Pitfalls:
  - Two centre clicks with no `advance` between are a double click (`docs/capabilities.md:477`). Step 7's cases that
    need two circles put an `advance` between their clicks, except the case that opens the dialog.
  - A `data-circles` written by a test with a repeated id reads `DuplicateKey` for the later circle. The fixture's
    `k` is unique by construction.

Circle Drawer, the stand's one canvas app, declares each circle it paints as a virtual node. Each circle reads as
`circle-canvas///c{id}` in the accessibility tree, the snapshot and its diff, the UI graph, `actions`, `layout` and
exploration, the reads the three earlier chunks built on fixture canvases. Its role is `Image` and its name
`Circle {id}, {d} px`. Its region is its bounding square cut to the canvas's content box (inputs#I2, F8). Its key comes from an id the
app gives each circle, never its index (security-plan · contract/stable-element-id/stability). The `data-circles`
attribute carries that id as a fourth field. The app's click is unchanged (F1 A): a click on a circle's node adds a
circle at its centre, a limit stated and witnessed.

- (a11y · stand) Each Circle Drawer circle reads as `circle-canvas///c{id}`, role `Image`, named `Circle {id}, {d} px`,

  (`stand_circle_nodes` a–b; a11y-plan · decision/snapshot-reads-the-tree).

body:
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_error_text.rs:27` — `use std::time::Duration;` reads `unused import` on the windows
  build (CI#45619756069's windows job log, line 735 as gh serves it).

  `x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc`, absent (P5 baseline of the plan's first entry 9, run dir `control-probes.md`).

6. **Coverage by virtual node (F5 B, CARRY 6).** In `packages/escher-driver/src/coverage.rs`:
   - `see` lists `click` for each graph node whose id holds `///` and whose owner's graph node carries a `click`
     handler, with `id` the virtual id and `owner` the canvas's id.
   - `handler_coverage` marks a virtual node's `click` reached where a replayed step is an accepted `click` naming its
     id. It reads the check's own steps (`Check::steps`, `Step::call`), the first `Replay::ran` of them, each accepted
     on replay.
   - A click on the canvas's id that lands inside a node's region counts the canvas's listener alone, a stated limit.
   - The module doc (`:9-12`) is restated. The coverage line keeps its form: ids, owner ids, event names and two
     counts (security-plan · decision/coverage-line-no-user-data).
   - The graph (`DioxusDocument::graph`) is not touched (F14 A).

12. **The controls**, implement's one-shot runs through `gate.py control`, each entered with its red reading:
    - C1: `CircleCanvas::virtual_nodes` returns an empty list → `stand_circle_nodes`'s
      `one_click_reads_a_circle_node_in_the_tree_and_the_snapshot` red.
    - C2: the region cut removed (the bounding square declared whole) → `at_twelve_and_a_hundred_circles_every_circle_reads_a_node` red, 3 refused at 100.
    - C3: the key from the circle's index in the list → `an_undone_circle_reads_stale_and_its_redo_keeps_its_id` red.
    - C4: the grouping's tie and nearest-centre rule replaced by «the last declared region holding the centre» →
      `each_circle_s_commands_carry_its_own_index` red (69 of 100 on the fixture, measured off-tree).
    - C5: `see`'s virtual-node arm removed → `a_kept_check_lists_the_unclicked_circle_s_click` red and
      `a_replayed_virtual_click_reaches_its_canvas_listener` red.
    - C6: `parse_circles` taking three fields again → `malformed_circle_text_reads_as_no_circle` red.
    
    Each control:
    - names the file and the text the edit removes, and its `case` by function name;
    - is reached past fail-fast by its entry's `--test` filter;
    - fires under `--timeout 1200`, sized to one blitz-tests target's compile and its cases. A `timeout` reading is
      read as not held, never as red.
    
    C1–C5's entry is the `stand_circle_nodes` gate, C5's second case the virtual-node gate, and C6's the seven_guis
    unit gate (keeps tests S4, test-plan · decision/mutation-controlled-tests).

13. **The CARRY 5 check:** the operator pass reads the CI windows job's log for the final HEAD and finds the warning
    `unused import: `snapshot`` 0 times (the last gate entry).

record.observed_gap: The renderer records a scene as serializable commands (fill, stroke, glyph run, layers, clips) and a scene serializer is in the workspace, used by the browser alone; no driver verb reads a canvas's content.

verification.acceptance: On the stand, in both layout modes, `canvas` answers Circle Drawer's draw commands at a summary and a full level, two reads byte-equal and equal to `stand_canvas_commands`' committed table on linux, windows and macOS (the CI read of the final HEAD); a click's line diff adds only the new circle's lines, each ending ` n={its index}`, and a resize's diff holds only lines carrying ` n=1`, naming its circle; every full-answer line ends ` n={k}` or ` n=-`, `k` the 1-based declaration index of the taken virtual node whose region holds the command's centre and lies nearest it, ties to the first declared, with 12 of 12 and 100 of 100 fixture circles reading their own index (`stand_circle_nodes`); `stand_canvas_lint` names a planted label past its region and reads no finding on the stand at boot, after a click and at 12 and 100 circles; the full dump's size at 1, 12 and 100 circles is stated in `docs/capabilities.md`; and every carrier's canvas answer holds the tag's number or `-` and no virtual id, name, glyph id or text (`stand_canvas_carriers`, `stand_masks_on_new_answers`).

record.observed_gap: A snapshot node needs an author id and a DOM element, so an agent sees a canvas as one opaque element; the UI graph reserves no id form for a non-DOM node; the layout verb reserves an app-canvas placing and the widget trait a commented accessibility tree.

verification.acceptance: On the stand, each Circle Drawer circle reads as a node with its key, role, name and region in the accessibility tree and the snapshot; a click on one acts on its circle and its diff names it; a covered, off-screen, disabled or removed one is refused with that cause; the UI graph, actions, handler coverage, layout explanation and exploration each list it; the circles are reached and acted on by keyboard.

body:
# Forks — 2026-11-25-circle-drawer-virtual-nodes (Circle Drawer's circles as virtual nodes)

Written at phase P4 on the operator's take-up direction (inputs#I1): every fork the plan meets, each with what crosses,
the rule it meets, each option's measured cost, its dependences, whose it is and the most conservative option that
still builds the entry. Default: none — nothing below is taken until the operator relays the answers.

Run dir: `.andromeda/runs/2026-11-25T16-18-13-phase/` · scope `doc:2026-11-25-circle-drawer-virtual-nodes/scope` rev 3 ·
research rev 1.

**Founder forks found: yes — F2 (C or D), F5 B, F6 B or C and F7 B are boundary widenings or reverse a word of his;
F1 B1 widens the declaration's form, the class of his F8 A.** Every other option is the operator's.

Terms searched across all seven masters for the widenings (`rec.py find --doc all --text …`): `canvas answer` (9 rows),
`virtual-node-crossing` (1), `served by no` (2), `served tasks` (10), `seven served` (6), `seven apps` (5),
`data-circles` (1), `coverage-line-no-user-data` (1), `не сейчас` (0 — the founder's serving word stands in the sidecar
alone, test-plan `amd-nasxjktn`).

How costs were measured: file and line reads at HEAD `a5d18f604`; the code-graph impact query (trace
`tree-query-2026-11-25-circle-drawer-virtual-nodes.json`, 59 rows); `stand_canvas_commands`' committed table; and the
fixture's circle sequence (`session_common::circles`) replayed off-tree for a 700 × 400 content box — at 12 circles 0
spill the box, 1 is under 16 px, 2 overlapping pairs, 2 centres under a later disc; at 100 circles 3 spill, 5 under
14 px, 7 under 16 px, 11 under 18 px, 109 overlapping pairs, 26 centres under a later disc. A size marked *derived* is
arithmetic on committed numbers, not a run.

---

## F1 — What a click on a circle's node does (v040-11 «a click on one acts on its circle and its diff names it»)

**Today.** `CircleDrawer`'s `onclick` (`circle_drawer.rs:267`) always pushes a new circle at the click point. The driver
acts on a virtual node at its region's centre (`execute.rs:794`). So a click on a circle's node adds a second circle on
top of it, and the diff names the new node, never the clicked one.

**What crosses / the rule it meets.** The stand app's behaviour; under B1 also the widget declaration's form
(`Widget::virtual_nodes`, `VirtualNodeDeclaration`, blitz-dom behind `custom-widget`, an escher addition). A selected
state crosses as the snapshot's existing closed `selected` reading — a closed value inside a ratified carrier, no
widening by the 2026-10-10 rule. The declaration's form was the delegate's F2 A (PROVISIONAL); its one added field so far,
`disabled`, was the founder's own F8 A.

| Option | What it does | Measured cost |
|---|---|---|
| A | App unchanged: a click on a circle's node adds a circle at its centre | 0 lines. v040-11's click clause stays unmet with no later owner: «Canvas keyboard path» claims v040-11 and inherits it |
| B1 | 7GUIs selection: a click inside a circle selects it (painted filled), adds none; `VirtualNodeDeclaration` gains `selected`, written to the tree, read as the snapshot's `selected` | blitz-dom `custom_widget.rs` +1 field and doc; `dioxus_document.rs` +3 lines (`:416`); the 8 declaration literals in 4 files (`custom_widget.rs`, `virtual_node.rs`, `fixtures/mod.rs`, `virtual_nodes_declared.rs`) take `selected: false`; app: a selection signal and its declared writes; the diff names the node, `differs: [selected]` |
| B2 | 7GUIs selection as B1, the state carried in the declared name («Circle 3, 40 px, selected») | app only; the diff names the node, `differs: [name]`; a state read from a name, not a state field — what an assistive technology hears is the name |
| C | A click on a circle opens its diameter dialog (today's double click) | app only; the diff names the dialog's nodes, not the circle — the clause stays unmet |

**Dependences.** F4: under B1/B2 a click on a circle another circle covers would select the top one, so F4 B makes that
refusal honest. F2/F3: selection repaints a fill, so a selected circle's commands change — CARRY 1's identity question.
`GRAPH_DRIVES` (`tests/common/mod.rs:352-360`): its double click lands on the circle its first drive added, so under
B1/B2 that first click of the pair selects rather than adds — the drives are re-read.

**Whose.** B1 — the founder's (the declaration's form, the class of F8 A). A, B2, C — the operator's (a stand change, no
engine change and no crossing).

**Most conservative that builds the entry:** A (the entry asks each circle a node, not a click semantics).
**Most conservative that also builds v040-11's click clause:** B2.

---

## F2 — The canvas answer grouped by virtual node (v040-10 «the commands grouped under the virtual node that covers them»; CARRY 1 «a changed command has no identity»)

**What crosses / the rule it meets.** security-plan `decision/virtual-node-crossing` (ratified): «the lint and canvas
answer hold none». security-plan `decision/canvas-content-crossing` (ratified): the canvas answer is closed words,
numbers and 64-bit digests. A node's key or id in it is author text, an open value set — a widening by the 2026-10-10
rule — and the playbook's `rul-izni57qv` (Boundary widening) escalates it. Rows reached by name: security-plan
`decision/virtual-node-crossing`, `decision/canvas-content-crossing`, `decision/kept-check-canvas-answer`,
`decision/cold-agent-canvas-to-provider`, `decision/no-screen-content-in-logs`; architecture
`decision/canvas-reading-diffable`, `decision/kept-check-never-logged`, `contract/command-span/never-fielded`;
test-plan `decision/socket-carries-commands`, `decision/typed-password-never-returned`; design-system
`decision/canvas-line-form-conventions` (the line form). Read as not reached: the snapshot, graph, actions and layout
rows (their carriers do not change).

**The shared mechanism (every option but A).** A command belongs to the last-declared taken node whose region holds the
centre of the command's bounds (declaration order read as paint order, a stated assumption); a layer push or pop, or a
command whose centre no region holds, belongs to none. A label is painted after every circle (`circle_drawer.rs:175`),
so grouping reads geometry, never position in the list. Each line keeps its paint order.

| Option | What a line carries | Measured / derived cost |
|---|---|---|
| A | No grouping (today) | 0. v040-10 stays pooled; CARRY 1 unbuilt |
| B | The covering node's 1-based index among the canvas's taken nodes in declaration order (`n=3`, `n=-` for none) — a number | `canvas.rs`, `json/canvas.rs`, `json_tests.rs`, `canvas_tests.rs`; *derived*: ~4 B × ~302 lines ≈ 1.2 KB on the 49,266-byte 100-circle dump, 6 parts stay 6. Identity is positional: stable on Circle Drawer (circles are appended, undo pops the last), not in general |
| C | The node's key alone | as B plus the key text; *derived* ~8–10 B a line ≈ 3 KB; widening |
| D | The node's id `{owner}///{key}` | as B plus the id; *derived* ~24 B a line ≈ 7 KB, 6 parts may become 7; the same class the founder ratified for graph, actions and layout (F13 A) |

Every option but A re-measures `stand_canvas_commands`' 17 committed rows and `stand_canvas_cross_os`' Circle Drawer
digests on linux, windows and macOS (one CI run), re-reads the kept-check replay guard
`a_kept_canvas_check_replays_green_and_a_flipped_digest_stops_it` and the two masked-answer checks, and moves
`docs/capabilities.md`'s 45 · 527 · 5,915 · 49,266.

**Dependences.** F1 (a selected fill changes a group's lines). The key form (F8) sets C's and D's size.

**Whose.** C, D — the founder's (a widening of a ratified crossing). A, B — the operator's (B adds numbers inside the
ratified canvas crossing).

**Most conservative that builds the entry:** B.

---

## F3 — A canvas label's region (CARRY 2, `cry-yf3l6oh7`)

**Today.** architecture `decision/canvas-label-region` (PROVISIONAL, the delegate's F2 A): a label reads against the
content box cut by each clip, layer or mask path and the element's clip region. On Circle Drawer every label sits inside
the one content-box clip, so none reads `truncated` at 12 or 100 circles.

**What crosses / the rule it meets.** Nothing new: a `truncated` finding already carries the ink box and region as
numbers (security-plan `decision/canvas-label-lint-crossing`). It meets layout-templates `decision/stand-lints-clean-at-boot`
(PROVISIONAL, delegate: Circle Drawer reads no canvas finding after a click or at 12 and 100 circles) and v040-10's
«reads clean on the stand».

| Option | A label reads against | Measured cost |
|---|---|---|
| A | Today's region (kept, its limit stated and witnessed on the stand) | 0 code; the CARRY is discharged as a kept limit |
| B | The painted shape under the label (the topmost fill whose bounds hold the label's centre) | `canvas_lint.rs`; on the fixture a label under ~14–16 px of diameter overflows: 0–1 finding at 12 circles, 5–7 at 100 — `stand-lints-clean-at-boot` and v040-10's clean reading move to measured counts, or the fixture's smallest diameter rises |
| C | The virtual node under the label (the last-declared region holding its centre), else today's region | as B, read from the declared regions instead of paint |

**Dependences.** F2 (C shares its region lookup). v040-10's «reads clean on the stand» holds under B/C only on the
stand's own click path (every circle 40 px) or a fixture with no circle under ~18 px.

**Whose.** The operator's (driver lint semantics, no crossing; the row it replaces is a delegate's).

**Most conservative that builds the entry:** A.

---

## F4 — `covered` by another virtual node (CARRY 3, `cry-llqauv26`)

**Today.** test-plan / a11y-plan `contract/refusal-cause/covered` (F12 A, delegate, PROVISIONAL): a virtual node reads
`covered` only by an element over its region's centre. `covered` has one caller, `action_point` (`execute.rs:968`), and
`actions` shares it through `check_target`, so a listed cause and a refusal stay one.

**What crosses / the rule it meets.** Nothing new crosses (a closed cause word). The meaning text of `covered` is one of
the eight fixed texts (ratified 2026-10-18); a clause was added to it once with its name, remedy and order unmoved
(test-plan `amd-4g5qmthy`).

| Option | What it does | Measured cost |
|---|---|---|
| A | Kept: elements alone cover | 0 code; a stand witness: a click on a circle under another acts on the top one's point |
| B | A later-declared taken node of the same canvas whose region holds the target's centre covers it | `execute.rs` `covered` (one function); the fixture's 26 of 100 (2 of 12) circles read `covered` in `click` and `actions`; on the stand's click path every driver click lands at the canvas centre (`docs/capabilities.md:477`), so all but the last of N centre circles read `covered` |

**Dependences.** F1 B1/B2 (without B, a click on a covered circle would select the top one). F5 (a refused click is never
reached).

**Whose.** The operator's (the row it changes is a delegate's; the cause's name, remedy and order are unmoved).

**Most conservative that builds the entry:** A.

---

## F5 — Handler coverage of a virtual node (CARRY 6, `cry-a2jh4k7x`)

**Today.** architecture `contract/handler-coverage/canvas` (F19 A, delegate, PROVISIONAL): a virtual node carries no
handler, a click on one counts its canvas's listener under the canvas's id (`coverage.rs:9-12`).

**What crosses / the rule it meets.** security-plan `decision/virtual-node-crossing` names the carriers of a virtual id
and the coverage line is not among them; security-plan `decision/coverage-line-no-user-data` holds the line to ids, owner
ids, event names and counts. A virtual id in the coverage line is a widening (obs-plan history `amd-coxkueit`:
«a virtual-node id appearing in it would be a widening»). The cap's own notes say F13 A took coverage; the row does not.

| Option | What it does | Measured cost |
|---|---|---|
| A | Kept: no virtual node listed; a click on one counted under `circle-canvas` | 0 code; a stand witness in `stand_handler_coverage` on Circle Drawer; v040-11's «handler coverage … each list it» stays unmet |
| B | Each virtual node of a canvas whose canvas holds a `click` listener lists `click` under its own id, owner the canvas, exercised when a replayed click landed on it | `coverage.rs` (`see`, the reached match), `stand_handler_coverage` tables, `virtual_nodes_in_every_read`'s `a_replayed_virtual_click_reaches_its_canvas_listener`; widening |

**Dependences.** v040-11 is not claimable by this chunk in any case (keyboard reach is «Canvas keyboard path»'s); under A
its coverage clause has no owner.

**Whose.** B — the founder's (a widening). A — the operator's.

**Most conservative that builds the entry:** A.

---

## F6 — The lint reads virtual nodes (CARRY 7, `cry-5zhvg5ed`)

**Today.** `lint.rs:229`: a canvas's virtual nodes are not linted (F20 A, delegate, PROVISIONAL); guard
`the_lint_holds_no_virtual_node`; security-plan `decision/virtual-node-crossing`: «the lint … hold[s] none».

**What crosses / the rule it meets.** A finding on a virtual node puts its id into the lint answer — a widening of the
ratified row above (`rul-izni57qv`). It also meets layout-templates `decision/stand-lints-clean-at-boot` and v040-10's
clean reading.

| Option | What it does | Measured cost |
|---|---|---|
| A | Kept: no virtual node linted | 0 code; a stand witness: Circle Drawer at 12 and 100 overlapping circles reads no finding |
| B | Virtual nodes linted for `off-screen`, `clipped` and `zero-size`, skipped by `overlap` on either side (the `in_select_box` precedent, `lint.rs:380`) | `lint.rs`; on the stand 0 findings (the app clips each region to its content box; a zero-area region is refused at declaration); widening |
| C | As B, and `overlap` between nodes too | the fixture's 2 overlapping pairs at 12 circles and 109 at 100 read `overlap`; every circle the stand's click path adds sits at the centre — the stand no longer reads clean; widening |

**Whose.** B, C — the founder's (a widening). A — the operator's.

**Most conservative that builds the entry:** A.

---

## F7 — The binary-level reading of a virtual node (CARRY 4, `cry-kou37dij`)

**Today.** Circle Drawer is served by no `escher-session` role: `session_host.rs` `TASKS` holds seven slugs, and
test-plan `contract/stand-boot/boot-circle-drawer` and architecture `contract/headless-stand/boot` say so — on the
founder's «A: не сейчас» at «Circle Drawer on a canvas» (test-plan `amd-nasxjktn`). The CARRY's premise «the first
served app to declare one» is false at HEAD (scope rev 3, premise-corrected).

**What crosses / the rule it meets.** Serving it puts Circle Drawer's screens — its circles' ids and names, canvas
answers — on the socket, the command line and MCP. Each content class there is already ratified
(`decision/virtual-node-crossing` names the socket and command-line line and MCP), but serving the app reverses the
founder's word. Rows reached: architecture `contract/headless-stand/boot`, `contract/escher-session/invocation`,
`contract/escher-session-cli/usage`, `decision/stand-readings-same-on-every-ci-os`; test-plan
`contract/stand-boot/boot-circle-drawer`, `contract/escher-session-command-line/start`,
`decision/cross-os-readings-by-answer-digest`, `contract/session-run/layout-answer`; layout-templates
`contract/escher-session-served-tasks/*` (a new row). Read as not reached: the cold-agent rows (`seven apps` in
`contract/cold-agent-tasks/stand`, `decision/cold-agent-prompt-names-no-ids`, `contract/cold-agent-verdict/passed`) —
the pipe's task lists its own apps and stays seven unless a later entry changes it.

| Option | What it does | Measured cost |
|---|---|---|
| A | Not served; CARRY 4 re-carried to «Cold-agent live run» (Epoch 6), the first run that could read it | 0 code |
| B | Circle Drawer served as the eighth task; a virtual node's id and name read on the binary's command-line stdout, through the socket host and from the `mcp` child; 0 needles of either in `host_log` / `mcp_log` at trace; no live run | `session_host.rs` (`TASKS` 7 → 8, a `Served` arm); `cli_commands`, `mcp_server`, `host_log`, `mcp_log`, seven_guis `tests/common/mod.rs` (a needle helper); `stand_cross_os_readings` gains Circle Drawer's rows (54 → 60, measured on three OSes) or states its exclusion; the rows above re-stated «seven» → «eight» |
| C | B and a cold-agent live run | B plus a live run (≤ 3 USD a firing on the founder's earlier cap, `decision/cold-agent-live-run-fired-once`) and the pipe's stand task taking an eighth app — the work of «Cold-agent live run», not this entry |

**Whose.** B, C — the founder's (they reverse his «A: не сейчас»; C also spends on a live run). A — the operator's.

**Most conservative that builds the entry:** A (the entry's text does not name the binary; the CARRY moves with a reason).

---

## F8 — A circle node's key, name, role and region (no crossing; the operator's leans)

- **Key** — leaned, settled by an artifact: an id the app gives each circle from a counter, carried to the widget as a
  fourth field of `data-circles`; the key `c{id}`. security-plan `contract/stable-element-id/stability` forbids an index
  key, as CRUD's rows are keyed by the person's id (layout-templates `amd-iapsmysj`). It changes the `data-circles` form
  the founder-ratified layout-templates `decision/circle-drawer-circles-painted-on-canvas` states (`x,y,d`).
- **Name** — lean «Circle {id}, {d} px» (its diameter, as painted), non-empty; it crosses the ratified name carriers.
- **Role** — contestable: `Button` (a click acts on it under F1 B), else `Image` (under F1 A). Operator's.
- **Region** — leaned: the circle's bounding square cut to the content box, so no circle is refused `RegionOutside`
  (3 of the 100-circle fixture spill today).

---

## F9 — How Circle Drawer names its role `Image` (met at P4 after the answers, inputs#I2; a lock move, so the phase stops)

**Found.** `VirtualNodeDeclaration.role` is an `accesskit::Role` (`packages/blitz-dom/src/node/custom_widget.rs:182`).
blitz-dom takes `accesskit` (optional, on through `custom-widget = ["dep:anyrender", "accessibility"]`,
`packages/blitz-dom/Cargo.toml:23`) but re-exports neither the crate nor `Role`: `pub use accesskit` reads 0 hits over
`packages` (`git grep -n "pub use accesskit\|pub extern crate accesskit\|pub use ::accesskit" -- packages`).
`examples/seven_guis/Cargo.toml` names no `accesskit`, and seven_guis' `Cargo.lock` entry lists none (`Cargo.lock:7765`).
So the app cannot write `Role::Image` (or any role but the default `Unknown`, through `Default`) as the tree stands. The
relay's standing line: «A lock move is not expected; if research meets one, stop» (inputs#I2).

| Option | What it does | Measured cost |
|---|---|---|
| A | seven_guis takes `accesskit = { workspace = true }` | `examples/seven_guis/Cargo.toml` +1 line; `Cargo.lock` seven_guis entry +1 line `"accesskit",` — no new package, no checksum; the `audit` leg and the lock probe run; a lock move |
| B | blitz-dom re-exports the role type beside the declaration: `pub use accesskit::Role as VirtualNodeRole` (or the crate) under `#[cfg(feature = "custom-widget")]` in `packages/blitz-dom/src/lib.rs:107` | `lib.rs` +2 lines and a doc line; no manifest, no lock; a public item on an engine crate, an escher addition flagged upstreamable like the trait; the `doc` leg runs |
| C | The role left `Unknown` (`Role::default()`) | 0 manifest lines; the snapshot reads each circle with role `unknown` — F8's `Image` not met |

**Dependences.** F8 (the role word). Nothing else in the plan moves with it.

**Whose.** A — the operator's (the relay names a lock move a stop, not a refusal; no new package or crossing). B —
the operator's (an additive public item behind the feature, the class of `Widget::virtual_nodes` itself, the delegate's
F2 A). C — the operator's.

**Most conservative that builds F8 as answered:** B (no manifest or lock line).

---

## Not a fork — what the intent already decides, reaching the founder at the wrap

Two founder-ratified standing rows say the circles reach no snapshot, tree or graph: a11y-plan
`decision/circle-drawer-canvas-pixels-only` and layout-templates `decision/circle-drawer-circles-painted-on-canvas`.
v040-11's requirement («Circle Drawer's circles are virtual nodes») makes both false, so the wrap re-states them on the
founder's confirm, under any answer above. test-plan `decision/reserved-graph-id-form`'s stand half («while the stand
declares no virtual node») is re-stated with them.

## The most conservative set that still builds the entry

F1 A · F2 B · F3 A · F4 A · F5 A · F6 A · F7 A, with F8's leans. It builds each circle as a node on the stand, its draw
commands grouped by node index, the stand checks, CARRY 5's fix, and witnesses each kept limit (CARRYs 2, 3, 6, 7) on
the stand. CARRY 4 moves to «Cold-agent live run». No founder word is needed beyond the wrap's re-statement above.
v040-10 becomes claimable; v040-11 stays pooled (keyboard reach, and its click and coverage clauses).

The `canvas` verb's full answer groups every command under the virtual node that covers it (v040-10's last open clause,
CARRY 1). Each line ends ` node={k}`, the 1-based index of the node among the canvas's taken nodes in declaration
order, or ` node=-` for none. Only numbers enter the ratified canvas crossing; no id or name does (F2 B; security-plan ·
decision/canvas-content-crossing). A changed command's removed and added lines carry one `node=`, which names its node;
the index is positional, a stated limit. The tag's key is `node`, a key no line holds: no command kind's line holds a
key twice (revision 1, inputs#I7 — the glyph line already writes `n` for its glyph count, `json/canvas.rs:220`).

4. **Commands grouped by node (F2 B, CARRY 1).** In `packages/escher-driver/src/canvas.rs`:
   - `Session::canvas` (`:270`) reads the canvas's declared nodes through `DioxusDocument::virtual_nodes`. A read that
     answers `NoCanvas` or `NotLaidOut` groups nothing.
   - The regions and the paint scale are handed to `read_commands` (`:305`).
   - Each command's bounds are read in the scene's frame and divided by the scale into CSS px of the content box. A
     fill or stroke uses its shape's bounding box under its transform, a glyph run the box of its glyph origins under
     its transform, a box shadow and an image their rect.
   - A command belongs to the taken node whose region holds the centre of its bounds and whose region's centre lies
     nearest it, ties to the first declared. A layer push or pop, or a command with no area or whose centre no region
     holds, belongs to none.
   - The reading carries each command's node as a 1-based index into the taken nodes in declaration order, or none.
   
   In `packages/escher-driver/src/json/canvas.rs`, `canvas_lines` (`:255`) ends every line ` node={k}` or ` node=-`
   after its form (spelled ` n=` by the run that did this step; step 14 respells it), in every canvas answer, declaring or not. `canvas_line_lengths` (`:280`) counts the tag, so parts still
   cut within the budget. The summary is unchanged. The command span and every log stay as they are
   (obs-plan · decision/canvas-read-opens-no-span, architecture · contract/command-span/never-fielded).

7. **The stand check, new** — `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_circle_nodes.rs`, one behaviour: Circle Drawer's circles
   as virtual nodes, both layout modes. Its tables are shared in `tests/blitz-tests/tests/common/mod.rs`, each with its
   row count asserted. It asserts its fixture's condition first (keeps arch S1–S5, tests S1–S5, a11y S1–S2, security
   S1–S2, obs S2/S4). Its cases:

     «Circle 1, 40 px» and that author id. The snapshot reads it with `bounds` equal to its region moved by the canvas's

   - (b) At 12 and at 100 circles of the fixture sequence (step 9's form), the snapshot lists 12 and 100 such nodes.
     None is refused: `virtual_nodes`' `refused` is empty. Each of the 3 circles that spill the box at 100 reads its
     cut region.

     naming it is refused `stale`. A redo brings `c2` back under the same id. A click after another undo reads `c3`.
     An id no screen read is refused `not-found`.
   - (d) Diffs: a click's diff adds the new node. A resize through the dialog changes `c1`, its diff naming `name` and
     `bounds` in `differs`.
   - (e) F1 A witness: a `click` on `circle-canvas///c1` is accepted, settles and adds a circle at its centre. Its diff
     adds `c2` and leaves `c1` unchanged.
   - (f) F4 A witness: with `c1` under `c2` at the centre, a click on `c1` is not refused `covered`.
   - (g) The other reads on Circle Drawer:

     - `actions` lists each with `click` and `layout` free of a cause, and `type`, `scroll`, `screenshot` and `canvas`
       `not-found`;
     - `layout` answers it placed `by: app` in `circle-canvas`;
     - an in-process `explore` with a budget of 40 reaches a path whose call clicks a `c{id}` id.
     
     The graph, actions and layout answers hold the id and never the name «Circle 1, 40 px».
   - (h) F6 A witness: at 12 and 100 fixture circles the lint reads no finding, and no finding id holds `///`.
   - (i) F3 A witness: the fixture's smallest circle at 100 (diameter under 14 px, 5 measured) has a label wider than its
     circle, and it reads no `truncated` finding: the label's region is the content box.
   - (j) The grouping:
     - After one click, the full answer's fill, stroke and glyph lines end ` node=1` and its layer lines ` node=-`.
     - At 12 and 100 fixture circles, each circle's fill, stroke and glyph lines end with its own index, for 12 of 12
       and 100 of 100 circles.
     - A resize's line diff holds only removed and added lines carrying ` node=1`: identity by node.
     - Positional limit witness: after an undo of `c2` and a new click, the new circle `c3` reads ` node=2`, the index
       `c2` held (as built: through the attribute, two circles apart — step 14's done-record, deviation 5).
   - (k) F5 B: a kept check on Circle Drawer clicks `circle-canvas///c1` after two canvas clicks. `handler_coverage`
     over it lists `circle-canvas///c2` `click`, owner `circle-canvas`, unexercised, and lists neither `c1`'s `click`
     nor the canvas's `click`. A second check clicking only the canvas lists both nodes' `click` unexercised (unix, as
     every recording check, tests S6 / test-plan history `amd-xliprnr6`).

- Disabled-ness is keyed one way since 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness (in every document, ratified by the founder): the `DISABLED` state (`:disabled`) reads the attribute's presence, and the pointer-move gate, `ClickTarget::Disabled`, `handle_click`'s walk gate, the Enter and Space activation and focusability read `ElementData::is_disabled` — that presence on a `button`, `input`, `select` or `textarea` alone (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18) — so `disabled="false"` and a bare `disabled` on a form control match `:disabled` and are not focusable, a bare `disabled` set after creation takes its focusability away, and a `<div disabled tabindex=0>` takes focus. dioxus-native-dom removes a falsy value of its 28 boolean attributes — upstream's `is_bool_attr` predicate since 2026-10-13-upstream-sync-polish-and-ship (`disabled`, `checked`, `hidden`, `inert` among them; a framework-written `inert: false` is removed, while a truthy `inert` (by presence on itself or an ancestor element) takes focusability, hits and the tree away from its subtree (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18) and Tab reaches the buttons under `inert: false`; HTML's focus fixup is built, in every document, so a node holding focus when it comes under `inert`, a subtree moved under an inert box included, gives focus up as the mutator flushes, no DOM `blur` or `focusout` firing; and a focused node that no longer shows gives focus up after each layout, no DOM `blur` or `focusout` firing, while a `display: contents` control and one beside a hidden sibling keep focus (ratified, the Tab walk's skip of unshown nodes remedying the Tab trap the post-layout fixup alone made; a control whose own `:focus-within` rule hides its container still takes Tab and loses focus at the next layout, a stated limit)), so a `hidden: false` element stays displayed, in the tree and in the snapshot; an attribute outside the list holding `false` is still written as `"false"`. The snapshot reads `enabled` by presence (on a virtual node the declaration's disabled flag, `enabled` false where declared disabled) — the driver's `disabled` refusal cause is stated on the same presence reading ("the element carries the `disabled` attribute, which the snapshot reads as not enabled") and is detected on it and on nothing else: the driver refuses a `click` or a `type` as `disabled` when the snapshot reads the element not enabled, with nothing dispatched and focus as it was, and acts on the same control once it reads enabled (`stand_act_disabled.rs`), and the driver's schema defines no role or name set of its own — `checked` a native checkbox's or radio's state, else, on a checkable role, the node's `toggled` reading (`True` true, `False` and `Mixed` false; ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18), and `value` from the element (a `select`'s `value` `BaseDocument::select_value` — the chosen option's value, for a `multiple` select its first chosen option's in tree order, nothing with none chosen — its options, its children and those under an `optgroup`, kept in the tree as `ListBoxOption` nodes, each `selected` from its chosen state, a closed drop-down's options under it with its select's client rect as their `bounds`, which the driver's visual lint leaves out of its overlap reading in every document with an open list's rows and groups, an open list's row reading its painted row's `bounds` (`Entry.in_select_box`, read through `closed_select_of` for a closed select's option and through `select_list_bounds` for an open list's row or group, never the role) — the stand's flight booker at boot no `overlap`, `stand_lint` reading `[0, 0, 0, 0]` — while a list box's rows and groups, `multiple` or of display size above 1, read their own client rects and its rows are linted as usual; a range input's `value` its current value since 2026-10-13-range-input-interaction — `ElementData::range_input_value`, the formatted value a key or a pointerdown moved, while its `value` attribute keeps the boot value; a password input's value reads the fixed mask `MASKED_VALUE` where it holds text and `""` where it holds none, a file input's where its `value` attribute is non-empty — and, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, a password's typed text is in no painted frame either: blitz-paint paints its value as bullets, its caret at the bullet of its caret index, in every document and through every renderer that paints with blitz-paint, windowed included (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-12), two values of one length painting byte-identical frames, focused or not, in both layout modes (`password_painted_masked.rs`); a click inside a field holding a value places the caret by the bullets — `click_password_input` lays out one U+2022 per character through `BaseDocument::layout_as_text_input`, finds the bullet under the point and moves the real editor to that character, so no width of the real characters reaches the caret: two values of one length read one index, in both layout modes (`password_caret_click.rs`; ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18); the windowed paint is not run; a textarea's typed text reads back as its `value`, proven on an in-file fixture where it is named by `aria-label`), and `focused` from the tree, and `clickable` (a `bool` after `focused`, true where the vdom walk's current listeners hold `click` and the element is no disabled form control; `Snapshot::to_text` writes the token `clickable` after `focused` only when true, and `Snapshot::diff` reads it as `Reading::Clickable`) — focus proven after a click, a Tab press and Shift+Tab (`stand_snapshot_state.rs`). record.title: Virtual nodes inside a canvas
record.requirement: An app declares nodes inside a canvas with an author key, role, name and region, and the driver treats them as elements across the snapshot, diff, click, refusals, UI graph, actions, coverage, layout and exploration; Circle Drawer's circles are virtual nodes
record.observed_gap: A snapshot node needs an author id and a DOM element, so an agent sees a canvas as one opaque element; the UI graph reserves no id form for a non-DOM node; the layout verb reserves an app-canvas placing and the widget trait a commented accessibility tree.

verification.acceptance: On the stand, each Circle Drawer circle reads as a node with its key, role, name and region in the accessibility tree and the snapshot; a click on one acts on its circle and its diff names it; a covered, off-screen, disabled or removed one is refused with that cause; the UI graph, actions, handler coverage, layout explanation and exploration each list it; the circles are reached and acted on by keyboard.
